joints.attack_plan: PHASE 1, before any blind_from read: from specification.yaml alone write and run one independent script (own code, standard library, outside the repository; exact integers and fractions; any real-valued tail at >= 50 significant digits per tail_checks) deriving: (a) counting table: for each (nv, neq) in S0-1 the D = 4 rows neq*C(nv,<=2) and columns C(nv,<=4), the D_reg counting rung as the index of the first non-positive coefficient of (1+z)^nv/(1+z^2)^neq, and the exact series coefficients up to it (S0-3), stating the D_reg convention used and every disagreement with the idea figures the specification quotes; (b) the (R, C) pairs of the seven C-FIX triples; (c) the size law per LA-7 (R_4*C_4*(C_4/64) exact-binomial, and the leading term 0.0417*l^11) at (23,8), (35,12) and the labelled extrapolation (131,44), the l = 44 memory figure, and l* as a function of a declared per-node loop constant c; state whether the specification alone fixes the loop-cost model l* needs, and if not record 'not derivable from the specification alone' instead of importing one; (d) the power table per S0-6: exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson 95 percent intervals for every x in 0..N, N in {60, 30, 20, 10}; zero-failure bounds at 60/60 and 20/20; the least N whose zero-failure CP95 upper bound on the miss rate is <= 2^-l for l = 8 and 12, compared with 3*2^l; the expected-count multiples 6 and 30 at N = 60 and 3/20; 0.025^(1/60) to >= 15 significant digits; (e) the stream rule from instance_sets alone: the complete ordered generator call sequence per (arm, cell) including the curve rule and its cap, the field-polynomial rule (LA-6), keep rules and caps, and the 13 seeds recomputed from seed_rule. Seal (phase_protocol.seal). PHASE 2: compare item by item with stage0/counting-table.yaml, size-law-and-lstar.yaml, power-table.yaml, stream-rule.yaml and selfchecks.json. Where I expect trouble, from the specification text: the D_reg convention and the (20,29) rung the specification itself leaves as '4 or 5'; the l* loop model; 3*2^l versus the exact zero-failure N; the leading-term constant (0.0417 in LA-7, 'about 0.04' elsewhere).
joints.breaking_artifact: A spec-derived value (row or column count, D_reg, series coefficient, CP95 bound, size-law entry, 0.025^(1/60), seed, call-sequence step) that differs from the producer worksheet, or a worksheet entry the specification yields no derivation for (imported or invented figure), each reported with both values and the derivation.

joints.attack_plan: PHASE 2. For each S0-k state the specification's condition, locate the record and code path that produced its 'ok' (selfchecks.json, implementation/run.py), and classify the pass as (i) tests the stated condition, (ii) tests a weaker condition (a file merely exists; a value is compared with itself or with the same formula that produced it; a figure copied rather than recomputed), or (iii) untested. A weaker or untested condition recorded as ok is a defect even when J1 finds the value right: J1 decides the value, J2 decides whether the gate was real. Per item: S0-1 must recompute D_reg and the counts and compare them with the idea figures; S0-2 is C-FIX; S0-3 must give exact coefficients at every planned cell (state which cells 'every planned cell' covers); S0-4 must state the exact PCG64 call order for every arm, the curve rule and the LA-6 field rule consistently with instance_sets, since INV-14's anti-steering purpose needs the order fixed before any draw; S0-5 needs both size-law forms, the l = 44 memory figure and an l* table over declared c with the idea's l* about 50 and its implied c; S0-6 needs exact CP95 for every x of each N and the zero-failure bounds. Report whether stages.stage_0.blocks_stage_1_until should have blocked Stage 1.
joints.breaking_artifact: An S0-k recorded ok whose implementation does not test the specification's condition, or a rule document missing an element S0-4, S0-5 or S0-6 requires, quoted with the specification clause and the missing element.
joints.joint: J2 -- STAGE-0 SELF-CHECK ADEQUACY. Each recorded S0-1..S0-6 pass tests the condition the specification states, so that 'all pass' licensed Stage 1 under blocks_stage_1_until.

C-PIN: enumerate the specification's C-PIN elements (sha256 AND git blob id of every pinned instrument and every archived input, i.e. the eight inputs.pinned_instruments and the five archived_m2_systems_for_c_base files; numpy 2.4.6; RLIMIT_AS 3 GiB set; src/semaev_tree.py sha256 and git blob 2281d6368a8fe28f9b23609ad5925a39dfd4890f) and mark each evidenced or not evidenced from the RUN RECORD (stage1/inputs.json, c-pin.json, environment.json, manifest, logs), not from code intent; compare every recorded hash with the specification table. C-SELF: for each of items (1)..(10) find the record of its execution; if c-self.json records a different check under the C-SELF name, report a control-identity defect, because a pass of a different check is not a pass of C-SELF. Byte recomputation of the pinned and archived paths is outside this card's read_scope (see known_limitations): do not read them; mark that element 'not recomputed: outside read_scope'.

phase_protocol.attempt_accounting: maximum_runs 1 is charged to the single phase-1 derivation script. Phase-2 sha256 recomputation of in-scope files and the proves-too-much checks on scratch copies are verification steps, not experiment runs; each is recorded with its exact command and output. No phase-1 value is recomputed, edited or re-sealed after exposure; a phase-1 error discovered later is reported beside the sealed value.
phase_protocol.attestation_contract: read-attestation.json holds the single canonical review_attestation: task_id TASK-20261003-c65b43; reviewer session identity and the policy/model actually served (requested review-adversarial at xhigh; fallback_used and its reason if any); joints_owned [J1, J2, J3, J4, J5]; verdicts as a mapping J1..J5 -> holds | breaks | inconclusive (holds = the producer's claim on that joint survives; breaks = a breaking_artifact exists; inconclusive = undecidable within scope); sources_read = the phase-1 reads only, by declaration of this plan (the list tools/check_review_independence.py compares with blind_from); blind_from_respected true only if no blind_from path was read, listed, grepped or inspected through git history before the seal; phase1_seal {sha256, utc}; phase2_sources_read = every post-seal read, never omitted; all_sources_read = their union; read_sibling_reports false; ptm_results per PTM id. report.json carries phase1_blind_rederivation (byte-identical to the sealed object), per-joint findings with evidence paths, the PTM table, the TASK-20261002-469111 completion_gate checklist, a defects list in a form the Coordinator can return to the Executor, and procedure_deviations.
phase_protocol.phase1: Fresh independent review-adversarial/xhigh session: not executor-7d2a86, not coordinator-7d2a86, not the dispatching session's own context. Read only phase1_allowed_reads. Do not read, list, grep or inspect through git log/show/diff any blind_from path (commit messages and diffs can carry values). Run the one J1 derivation script outside the repository and the proves-too-much objects that need no producer bytes (PTM-1 on the reviewer's own triples, PTM-3, PTM-4, PTM-5, PTM-7 as synthetic inputs). Record script source and sha256, command, Python version, stdout/stderr and every derived value as the phase1_blind_rederivation object destined for report.json.
phase_protocol.phase2: After the seal: read phase2_reads, compare with the sealed phase-1 values, and work J2-J5, PTM-2, PTM-6 and PTM-1 against the producer's triples. Read every producer byte at commit f920583227 (the snapshot's content binding). Permitted: sha256 of in-scope files. Not permitted: running the producer's launcher or checker, any closure, reading outside read_scope, writing anywhere but the two write_scope files.
phase_protocol.seal: Before the first phase-2 read, compute the sha256 of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators ',' and ':') of the phase1_blind_rederivation object and record it with a UTC timestamp as phase1_seal in read-attestation.json and in the session output. The archived report.json must contain that object unchanged; recomputing the digest from the archived file must reproduce phase1_seal, which the Coordinator checks in TASK-20261003-954a71.

proves_too_much.failure_signature: Each known-false object is rejected by the reviewer's own check, with the perturbation and the rejecting output recorded in report.json before the real artifacts are judged by the same check. A check that accepts any known-false object is defective, and every joint verdict resting on it is 'inconclusive', never 'holds'.
